option_checks.evidence: Focus-directed ray reflects parallel to principal axis in the explicitly paraxial concave model.
Curvature-center-directed incidence is along the local radius/normal and retraces; off-axis condition excludes the axial degeneration needed to make it parallel.
Principal axis is the pole's local normal; equal-angle reflection makes the two paths symmetric about that axis.
Off-axis parallel ray meets away from the pole and focuses approximately at F rather than retracing its nonnormal incident line.
A focus-directed off-axis ray is not a curvature-radius normal; it reflects parallel, not back along itself.
Local normal incidence at an actual reflecting surface returns along the incident line. This rule itself is exact local reflection.
The off-axis incident ray at P reflects obliquely and symmetrically about OP. It does not become the axial line through P and O.
Parallel incidence focuses approximately at the real concave focus within the stated paraxial model.

Three reflected rays can cross at the real image, but the option also asserts necessity of all three and insufficiency of any two. Two distinct noncoincident paths already determine the image point here.
There is no reflecting material in the central hole; the pole-directed traversing ray cannot supply an actual reflected constraint.
Any two of the three actual, pairwise noncoincident reflected paths intersect at the paraxial real-image point. Excluding the hole ray satisfies the original availability limit.
One line alone leaves infinitely many possible locations and does not uniquely determine a point without another constraint.
